title: Swimmer Archie Goodburn Will Carry the Rugby Ball for Scotland
summary:
Archie Goodburn is a champion swimmer from Edinburgh, Scotland. Next month, he will carry the match ball onto the field for Scotland's rugby game against Australia at Murrayfield stadium. More than 60,000 fans will be there.

Goodburn is 25. He holds the Scottish record for the 50-metre breaststroke and has won a European bronze medal. In 2024, doctors found a rare brain tumour. After surgery, he returned to racing. He also campaigns for better treatment and more research for people with brain cancer. He has taken that campaign to Prime Minister Andy Burnham and to Scotland's First Minister, John Swinney.

At school, Goodburn played rugby as a blindside flanker. “This means the absolute world to me,” he said. At age 12, he sang a solo for 10,000 people at the Edinburgh Military Tattoo. This crowd will be six times bigger. The match is on Sunday, November 15, and fans can donate to Brain Tumour Research and the Astro Brain Tumour Fund.
why_it_matters: Goodburn shows that coming back from a serious illness can also become a way to help other people facing the same challenge.
